metadata.description: How to fetch external data: use the fetch_url safe operation, never import urllib/requests in relaxaicode

context.domain_knowledge:
# Fetching external data (fetch_url recipe)
When the user asks for information you do NOT already have and that lives OUTSIDE Odoo — a public web page, a REST/JSON API, weather, prices, exchange rates, live status, timetables — you obtain it with the `fetch_url` safe operation.
NEVER write relaxaicode that imports `urllib`, `requests`, `http` or `socket`: those are blocked and the code is rejected before it runs. `relaxaicode` is a read-only Odoo sandbox with NO network access — it is for database data, not for the web.
## The pattern (imitate this)
1. If unsure whether the domain is allowed, read the `url_whitelist` resource first with `fetch_native_mcp_resource`. 2. Call `propose_safe_operations` with a `steps` list of `fetch_url` steps. Each step needs: `op = "fetch_url"`, a full `url`, and optionally `method` (`GET` default; also `HEAD`, `OPTIONS`, or `QUERY` with `body` + `content_type`). Safe methods only — no POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE here. 3. When the fetch returns, answer using ONLY the data in that result and cite the URL as the source. Never invent figures. 4. For authenticated or mutating HTTP against a known API, use `api_call` on a registered external server (MCP/OpenAPI), not `fetch_url`.
## Worked example
User: "What is the current USD→EUR exchange rate?"
WRONG — this is blocked, never do it:
import urllib.request, json raw = urllib.request.urlopen("https://api.example.com/rate?base=USD").read() result = json.loads(raw)
RIGHT — call `propose_safe_operations` with these arguments:
{ "steps": [ {"op": "fetch_url", "url": "https://api.exchangerate.host/latest?base=USD&symbols=EUR", "method": "GET"} ] }
Then read the returned JSON `body` and reply with the rate, citing the source.
## Good habits - BATCH: put several URLs as several steps in ONE `propose_safe_operations` call (they confirm and run together) instead of one call per URL. - Prefer JSON APIs: `fetch_url` is a plain HTTP request with no JavaScript, so single-page-app pages return empty HTML shells. - Whitelisted domains auto-confirm; other domains wait for a human click. - Safe query WITH a body (RFC 10008): use `"method": "QUERY"` plus `"body"` and `"content_type"` — for APIs whose read endpoint expects the query in the request body. QUERY is safe/idempotent like GET; it is NOT a POST. - Need a real POST or arbitrary custom headers? `fetch_url` cannot do it — use a registered external API server via `api_call` (MCP or OpenAPI), or tell the user it is out of scope. Never fall back to importing an HTTP library.
